title: lore check reports a profile whose declared sources cannot fit its max_tokens budget (DEC-11: warning for one release, then the error)
description:
A profile whose declared sources cannot fit its max_tokens budget makes lore's pack assembler drop declared sources, mark the pack truncated true with per-source omitted-by-budget, and EXIT 0. So a repository whose profiles declare more than their budgets hold runs narrowed packs and nothing says so -- a silent absence with a green exit. Found in the field, not theorised: ward-cli WCLI-25 (opum-ai/ward-cli#43) measured 16 of 16 packs complete before a change and 16 of 16 truncated after it, all at exit 0, with the documentation pack dropping its threat-model ADR on a generic task. The condition is capacity-driven -- declared sources against max_tokens -- and the same across four task texts, so it is checkable statically: no task string, no compile.

RULED by DEC-11 (opum-ai/opum-agent, .quest/planning.json at origin/main 0c61324, read there rather than taken on relay): the operator decided first-party via AskUserQuestion in the opum-doc session, 2026-09-29, relayed by opum-doc (correlation R-2026-09-29-01) and received by opum-agent at about 02:45Z. Option A: GATE IN lore check. A profile whose declared sources cannot fit its max_tokens budget becomes a lore check error, shipped FIRST AS A WARNING for one release so external users are not turned red without notice, and THEN AS THE ERROR. It authorises the pair release the change rides in (constitution Article 3). OPAG-714 is the paired audit half -- sdlc-audit reports truncated packs across the fleet -- and proceeds either way; it is fleet-only coverage, which is why the gate lives in lore. SCOPE: any lore check behaviour other than warning-then-error on capacity is a design change and goes back to opum-agent for the operator, not a reuse of this approval.

Filed on opum-agent's dispatch (cross-session, 2026-09-29T02:51Z). Queued after LCLI-639 and LCLI-640; it does not preempt either.

acceptanceCriteria.text: `lore check` reports, from the profile declaration alone, that a profile's declared sources cannot fit its max_tokens budget -- naming the profile, its budget and the sources that cannot fit -- and ships as a WARNING in the next pair release (DEC-11)
The flip to an error is a one-line, reviewable change, landed in the release AFTER the warning's and held as an explicit release step (DEC-11's warning-then-error ordering), not left to memory

A test proves the check warns on a deliberately over-declared fixture profile and stays silent on one that fits; a mutation control shows the capacity comparison is the clause doing the work (removing it reddens exactly the capacity cases); and the check prints how many profiles it read, so its clean answer cannot be a zero-input artifact

lore-cli's own profiles do not warn, each over-capacity profile made to fit by the declared-set measurement -- either its max_tokens raised to hold its complete declared set, or its declared sources narrowed to what its budget holds, chosen per profile -- with the pack size accepted recorded against the coverage dropped, per profile (opum-agent ruling 2026-09-29 under DEC-11's strict reading; OPAG-33's swept sizing is superseded, and the reason is capacity rather than the sweep)
bun test and bun run lore check exit 0; a reviewer pass covers the change

plan: 1. Core: task-free capacity measurement in src/core/agent-context.ts -- render the COMPLETE declared set (pins + every candidate of every declared source, no task, no query section) and compare to max_tokens; attribute in declaration order the sources that cannot fit. Reuses the compiler's own item/candidate/assemble internals so the size is the compiler's size, not a second implementation.
2. Rule: add 'agent-profile-capacity' to core/check.ts with a findings builder and ONE exported severity constant -- DEC-11's flip to an error is that single line (LCLI-646 holds the schedule).

3. Wire into src/commands/check.ts beside the existing loadAgentProfiles/validateAgentProfileReferences seam; add agentProfileCounts (profiles read / over capacity) to CheckReport and print it, so a clean answer cannot be a zero-input artifact.

4. Tests: over-declared fixture warns; fitting fixture silent; mutation control removing the capacity clause reddens exactly the capacity cases; the read count is printed; severity flows to the exit code (warning -> 0, --strict -> 6).
5. AC4: measure all four profiles, then make each fit by raising its budget or narrowing its declared sources, chosen per profile, recording the pack size accepted against the coverage dropped.
6. Docs: cli-contract (rule list, report field, exit semantics) and the agent-profile spec/runbook; bun test and bun run lore check exit 0.
7. Reviewer pass over the change (AC5), then close with the evidence.
implementationNotes:
MEASUREMENT carried over from LCLI-640 (2026-09-29), recorded here rather than left on the other record because AC4 depends on that profile's budget and because it is a trap for this task's implementer. Nothing here starts this task or changes its scope.

The capacity condition this task gates on is static and task-independent, but a PER-TASK omission is NOT evidence of it. The two must not be conflated when the check is implemented.

Measured on the bundle as LCLI-640 leaves it, with the new documentation profile at max_tokens 20000 and 10 declared sources, compiled against four realistic documentation tasks: the omitted-source counts were 5, 1, 0 and 0. Two of the four tasks omitted NOTHING, so that profile is not over capacity -- and the first task nonetheless omitted five declared sources (reference/lore-cli-documentation-ownership, reference/operate-autonomous-lore-cli-documentation-campaigns, adr/0010-multi-consumer-docs-layer, reference/consumer-compatibility, runbooks/agent-profile-operation, every one scoring at or below 4.16). That is the task-ranked mechanism working as designed, not a capacity defect. An implementation that compiles a pack for some task string and warns when anything comes back omitted-by-budget would therefore false-positive on lore-cli's own documentation profile and would fail AC4. The check has to compute capacity from the declaration alone -- declared sources against max_tokens, with no task string and no compile -- which is what the description already specifies. This measurement is the reason to keep it that way.

SECOND MEASUREMENT, which the capacity comparison must survive: the omission curve is NOT monotone in max_tokens, so "does everything fit" is not a monotone predicate in the budget. On the first task above, 20000 selected 23 of 80 ranked blocks while 20500 selected only 5; the larger budget admitted one large high-scoring block whole ("Release publishing > Steps > 3. Cut a release", score 8.480238) and it consumed the room several smaller blocks had been using. The full thirteen-budget table is on LCLI-640's evidence note. A capacity test expressed as a monotone size comparison is unaffected by this; a capacity test measured by compiling packs is not, and can move the wrong way as the budget is raised.

SECOND MEASUREMENT, and it bears on whether AC4 is satisfiable as written. Measured 2026-09-29 while closing LCLI-640, on origin/dev at a72f580f.

AC4 requires that "lore-cli's own profiles do not warn -- OPAG-33's swept budgets hold, with LCLI-640's documentation profile included -- captured on the current bundle." Under the reading of "cannot fit" that this task's own description gives (declared sources against max_tokens, capacity-driven, task-independent), ALL FOUR of this repository's profiles are over capacity and would warn. Measured, task text "review this change", each profile at its own declared budget:

  profile         budget  truncated  tokens  omitted
  implementation  20000   true       19956   4 of 14
  review          18000   true       17950   6 of 14
  verification    16000   true       15996   1 of 8
  documentation   20000   true       19976   2 of 11

`truncated` is true for every one, and each names the sources it dropped. Measured the other way -- the same four profiles compiled at `--max-tokens 200000`, where every declared source fits -- the complete declared sets are 102597, 57555, 88853 and 57134 tokens against budgets of 20000, 18000, 16000 and 20000. So the budgets are 2.9x to 5.6x SMALLER than the evidence those profiles declare.

This is not an artifact of LCLI-640's profile: implementation, review and verification are OPAG-33's swept budgets, and they show it too. OPAG-33 chose those numbers by sweeping for the point where no source scoring >=9 is fully omitted -- a task-ranked subset allowance -- and explicitly measured that "raising the budget alone plateaued at four omissions, which is PLAN.md 6.4's other diagnosis -- sources too broad, not only max_tokens too low". So OPAG-33's budgets are correct FOR WHAT THEY WERE SIZED TO DO and are over capacity for what AC4 appears to require.

THE PRECEDENT THIS TASK INHERITS, read by ref rather than relayed. ward-cli WCLI-25 (`.quest/completed/WCLI-25.json` at ward-cli origin/dev, 35b40b1) is where this rule was worked out, and its model is the strict one: a profile's budget must HOLD ITS COMPLETE DECLARED SET. Its notes record the independent review forcing that correction -- declaring every ADR in every profile without raising budgets made "16 of 16 packs truncated" and dropped the P0 threat model from the documentation pack on every task at exit 0 -- and the fix in two halves: budgets raised to hold what each profile declares (documentation 20000, the other three 17000, each at least 4500 tokens above its complete pack), and a truncation assertion added to the check. Its stated justification is the distinction this task's description also draws: with the declared set fixed and the budget under it, 16 of 16 combinations truncated and 16 of 16 did not once the budget held the set, "so the flag is capacity-driven while which sources drop is task-driven".

That precedent is coherent, and it is the one that makes AC1 well-defined and statically checkable. It is also, applied literally here, incompatible with AC4: it would require lore-cli's four budgets to rise to roughly 57000-103000 tokens, a 3-6x increase, and it would make every one of this repository's profiles warn until they do.

NOT DECIDED HERE, deliberately. Which of the two readings the DEC-11 ruling intends -- strict capacity (budgets must hold their declared sets, as ward-cli implements) or rank-based sufficiency (OPAG-33's >=9 test, which lore-cli's budgets satisfy) -- changes both the check and four budget values, and this task's own SCOPE says any lore check behaviour outside warning-then-error-on-capacity goes back to opum-agent. Raised there as an A/B packet rather than resolved locally or absorbed into a task here. Also NOT measured: whether OPAG-33's budgets could be raised to hold their complete sets without the profiles ceasing to be distinct evidence sets, which is the objection ward-cli's first draft raised against the strict reading and then measured through rather than assumed.

FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP: do not implement AC1 from the description alone and then discover AC4 fails, and do not satisfy AC4 by widening "fit" to something weaker than the check's own name promises. Both are the failure this note exists to prevent.

RULING RECEIVED AND APPLIED (opum-agent, cross-session, 2026-09-29). This answers the open question in the note above; nothing here is my judgement about which reading is right.

DEC-11 ITSELF SETTLES IT, read by ref rather than taken from the relay: opum-agent origin/main `.quest/planning.json`, decision DEC-11 (status accepted). Its outcome field reads, verbatim: "ACCEPTED: OPTION A, GATE IN LORE CHECK. ... A profile whose declared sources cannot fit its max_tokens budget becomes a lore check error. It ships first as a warning for one release, then as the error." and "SCOPE: this approves the option text as written in this record. Any lore check behaviour other than warning-then-error on capacity is a design change and goes back to opum-doc, not a reuse of this approval." So the strict capacity check is the approved behaviour and rank-based sufficiency is excluded -- not a new decision, the one already taken.

AC POSITION 4 AMENDED, which is the item the ruling calls "AC index 3" (the record's 0-based index; the flag takes the 1-based position, so the two differ by one here). It read "lore-cli's own profiles do not warn -- OPAG-33's swept budgets hold, with LCLI-640's documentation profile included -- captured on the current bundle." That middle clause was a prediction written into the task at filing, and the measurement above refuted it, so the criterion was corrected rather than the check being inverted to protect it. It now reads: lore-cli's own profiles do not warn, each over-capacity profile made to fit by the declared-set measurement -- max_tokens raised to hold its complete declared set, or declared sources narrowed to what its budget holds, chosen per profile -- with the pack size accepted recorded against the coverage dropped, per profile. Amended with `--if-revision` pinned to the pre-edit revision; no conflict. Positions 1, 2, 3 and 5 are unchanged.

OPAG-33'S SIZING IS SUPERSEDED, AND THE REASON IS CAPACITY, NOT THE SWEEP. Recording this here because the ruling asks for it explicitly and because the two are easy to conflate. OPAG-33's budgets were swept to the point where no source scoring >=9 is fully omitted -- a task-ranked subset allowance, and a correct answer to the question OPAG-33 was asked. They are wrong for the question DEC-11 asks, which is whether a profile's DECLARED set fits its budget at all. Measured: implementation declares 102597 tokens of evidence against a 20000 budget, review 57555 against 18000, verification 88853 against 16000, documentation 57134 against 20000 -- 2.9x to 5.6x over. So the sweep did not fail and does not need re-running; it was answering a different question. Nothing about OPAG-33's numbers is being retracted; they are simply no longer the sizing criterion.

THE NON-MONOTONE OMISSION CURVE IS WHY "SWEEP UNTIL IT FLATTENS" IS UNSAFE, and it is the reason this repository cannot simply re-sweep its way to budgets that fit. Measured on LCLI-640 and confirmed through two independent readers (the plain catalog and the --json envelope): on one task, budget 20000 selected 23 of 80 ranked blocks while 20500 selected 5 -- 500 tokens more, 18 blocks fewer. `context` ranks COMPLETE heading/top-level-block records, so a larger budget can admit one large high-scoring block whole and it consumes the room several smaller blocks were using (measured: `Release publishing > Steps > 3. Cut a release` enters at 8.480238). The budget is documented as a ceiling, so this is contract-compliant and not a defect to file; the consequence is narrower and worth stating plainly: the curve does not converge, 20000 was a local optimum rather than a plateau, and any repository sizing a profile budget by sweeping to where omissions stop is measuring a function that is not monotone. The full thirteen-budget table is on LCLI-640's evidence notes.

EXECUTION, MINE UNDER DEC-11 AND NOT YET STARTED. Per profile, either raise max_tokens to hold the complete declared set or narrow the declared sources to what the budget holds, and record the pack size accepted against the coverage dropped. The tension to weigh, stated so it is not rediscovered late: raising implementation to ~102597 and verification to ~88853 produces very large evidence packs to hand a subagent, while narrowing their declared sets drops coverage that OPAG-33 deliberately selected -- so this is a real trade per profile rather than a mechanical bump, and the numbers above are what it is traded against.

ALSO RECORDED, so the right task owns it: the runbook fix for choosing max_tokens is LCLI-644, confirmed by the ruling as its home. This task does not carry it.

IMPLEMENTED AND MEASURED (2026-09-29). Branch feat/LCLI-642-agent-profile-capacity-check, off origin/dev d19ce1c8.

DEFINITION, and the trap it avoids. The check measures a profile's COMPLETE DECLARED SET -- every candidate of every pinned/sources reference, plus the auto-pinned Constitution -- rendered by the same code the pack compiler uses, with no task and no query section, and compares it to max_tokens. It compiles no task pack and takes no task string, so it cannot fire on the task-ranked omission a real pack shows: measured on this bundle, the documentation profile drops 5 declared sources on one realistic task, which is a different question from capacity (this record's first note). Attribution names the sources that cannot fit in DECLARATION order -- the compiler's own order when a task matches no candidate -- and both the finding text and the docs say so, rather than implying a per-task omission set.

MEASURED, declared set vs budget, on origin/dev d19ce1c8 BEFORE this change -- the numbers the check prints:
  implementation  101259 / 20000  (12 of 13 sources could not fit)
  review           56765 / 18000  (11 of 13)
  verification     87664 / 16000  (6 of 7)
  documentation    56526 / 20000  (5 of 10)

AC POSITION 4 DECISION, per profile -- RAISE, not narrow, given as pack size accepted against coverage dropped:
  implementation  max_tokens 106000  accepted 102377 tokens (251/251 candidates, truncated:false)  coverage dropped: none
  review           62000             57469 (117/117)                                             none
  verification     93000             88689 (219/219)                                             none
  documentation    62000             57107 (80/80)                                               none
Why raise: narrowing to the old budgets would have dropped most of each profile's curated declared set -- for implementation cli-surface (28k), architecture, tech-stack and 9 ADRs; for verification both release-truth (31.5k) and the release-publishing runbook (28k), which are its actual subject. The declarations were curated deliberately (OPAG-33, LCLI-640) and DEC-11's strict reading makes the declaration the contract, so the budget moves rather than the evidence. Headroom is >=4500 tokens per profile (the ward-cli WCLI-25 precedent) and covers both document growth and a real task's bundle-wide query section, which is NOT part of the declared-set measurement. Real-task packs at the new budgets: all four compile with truncated:false and every candidate selected.

VERIFICATION (all measured, not asserted).

- bun test: 4807 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail (4808 tests across 134 files), including the new test/check-agent-profile-capacity.test.ts (8 cases). bun run lore check exits 0 with 0 errors and 0 warnings and prints "Agent profiles: 4 read, 0 over capacity". bun run lint exits 0 with the same 4 warnings and 1 info dev already carries -- confirmed by re-running lint with this branch's changes stashed, which reported the identical set. bun run typecheck clean.

- MUTATION CONTROL (AC position 3's third measurement, the fleet's mutate-the-check rule): mutating the comparison -- `overCapacity: declaredTokens > profile.maxTokens` to `false` in src/core/agent-context.ts -- reddens EXACTLY 4 of the 8 cases: both [capacity] cases, the over-capacity [count] case, and the [severity] command case; the fitting profile, the unmeasurable profile and the builder-level cases stay green. Predicted 3 before running, measured 4: the extra red is the [severity] case, whose command half asserts that a finding exists, which the tag description in the file header does not account for. Recorded rather than tidied, because the prediction is only useful if it is the one made before the run.

- THE FLIP IS ONE LINE, MEASURED RATHER THAN CLAIMED (AC position 2's mechanism half): with AGENT_PROFILE_CAPACITY_SEVERITY flipped from "warning" to "error", the suite stays 8 of 8 GREEN with NO test edit, a fixture repository whose profile is over capacity exits 6 with "1 error" from `lore check`, and this repository's own check still exits 0 because its profiles now fit. Restored to "warning" afterwards and re-verified by grep and a green run. The schedule half of that criterion is held by LCLI-646 (filed before this work, dependent on this task) and by the release runbook's new "Held release steps" section, which is where a release cutter reads it.

- POSITIVE CONTROL ON THE INSTRUMENT: the fixture cases assert that the fixture's declared set really is over its budget -- measureAgentProfileCapacity returns overCapacity true, the large source fits:false, the small source fits:true -- so the warning cases cannot pass on a fixture that never crossed the line.

- "IS THE CLEAN ANSWER A ZERO-INPUT ARTIFACT?" answered three ways: `agentProfileCounts` is emitted in the report whenever the repository declares profiles, the printed report carries the same counts, and a profile whose declared reference does not resolve in this bundle (a member::id reference that is meaningful only under --workspace) is counted as `unmeasurable` rather than silently treated as fitting.

- DOCS, so the contract is not only in code: cli-contract's check.report row and its exit-6 row, the agent-profile spec's max_tokens bullet, the release runbook's "Held release steps", and CHANGELOG [Unreleased]. LCLI-644's runbook section should cross-reference the rule; noted there rather than done here, because that section is that task's deliverable.

- ONE THING THIS RECORD DOES NOT CLAIM: the "ships in the next pair release" half of AC position 1 is a release-time fact. What this PR puts on dev is the warning-tier behaviour, with the severity constant naming the schedule; nothing in it can make the release happen, and LCLI-621/LCLI-622 stay Paused on the release gate.
